chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It is not befitting that the free man marries the slave woman today. Rather, that was when Allah Mighty and Majestic said: 'And whoever among you has not within his power ampleness of means', and the ampleness of means is the dower, and a dower of the free woman today is a dower of the slave girl or even less.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a free man marrying a slave woman in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling in *al-Kafi* to clarify that the permissibility of a free man marrying a slave woman, originally linked to poverty in Quran 4:25, is contingent on the economic disparity between the two groups. The hadith argues that since the dower (*mahr*) for a free woman today is often equivalent to or less than that of a slave woman, the condition of 'lack of means' is no longer distinctively applicable, thereby rendering the marriage less befitting in contemporary contexts. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the dynamic application of *talw* (ample means) based on socio-economic realities rather than rigid literalism.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Iibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It is not befitting that the free man marries the slave woman today. But rather, that was where Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Says [4:25] And whoever among you has not within his power ampleness of means, and the ampleness of means is the dower, and a dower of the free woman today is a dower of the slave girl or even less’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from certain persons of our people who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

It is not proper today for a free man to marry a slave- girl. It was permissible as Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has said, ‘If one cannot find resources. . . .’ [4:25] Resources is a reference to mahr (dower). Today mahr (dower) is like the mahr (dower) of slave-girls or less.’”
